thread.title: Apple Leading Nasdaq Higher, Trade Worries Weighing On Dow - U.S. Commentary

title: Apple Leading Nasdaq Higher, Trade Worries Weighing On Dow - U.S. Commentary
text:
Apple Leading Nasdaq Higher, Trade Worries Weighing On Dow - U.S. Commentary 8/2/2018 12:01 PM ET
After ending the previous session on opposite sides of the unchanged line, the major averages are turning in another mixed performance during trading on Thursday. While the tech-heavy Nasdaq is moving higher for the third straight day, the Dow is adding to yesterday's loss.
Currently, the major averages remain mixed. The Dow is down 109.19 points or 0.4 percent at 25,224.63, while the Nasdaq is up 39.95 points or 0.5 percent at 7,747.23 and the S&P 500 is up 0.94 points or less than a tenth of a percent at 2,814.30.
The Nasdaq continues to be supported by a notable advance by shares of Apple (AAPL), with the tech giant jumping by 2.5 percent to a new record high after soaring by 5.9 percent on Wednesday.
Apple briefly hit a $1 trillion market capitalization as traders continue to react positively to the company's upbeat fiscal third quarter results and guidance.
On the other hand, trade concerns are weighing on some of the other Dow components after President Donald Trump's administration confirmed reports it is considering raising the rate of tariffs on Chinese imports.
U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said Trump has directed him to consider increasing the proposed tariff rate on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods to 25 percent from the previously announced 10 percent.
"The Trump Administration continues to urge China to stop its unfair practices, open its market, and engage in true market competition," Lighthizer said. "We have been very clear about the specific changes China should undertake."
He added, "Regrettably, instead of changing its harmful behavior, China has illegally retaliated against U.S. workers, farmers, ranchers and businesses."
In response, China reiterated its threat to retaliate, with the Chinese Ministry of Commerce declaring the communist country fully prepared to defend its dignity and the interests of its people.
Overall trading activity has remained somewhat subdued, however, as traders seem reluctant to make significant moves ahead of the release of the Labor Department's closely watched monthly jobs report on Friday.
Employment is expected to increase by 190,000 jobs in July, while the unemployment rate is expected to edge down to 3.9 percent.
A day ahead of the release of the monthly report, the Labor Department released a report showing a modest increase in initial jobless claims in the week ended July 28th.
The report said initial jobless claims inched up to 218,000, an uptick of 1,000 from the previous week's unrevised level of 217,000. Economists had expected jobless claims to rise to 220,000.
A separate report from the Commerce Department showed factory orders climbed by 0.7 percent in June, matching economist estimates.
Sector News
Most of the major sectors are showing only modest moves in mid-day trading, contributing to the lackluster performance by the broader markets .
Steel stocks continue to see substantial weakness, however, with the NYSE Arca Steel Index plunging by 2.7 percent. The sell-off comes as traders worry about the impact of the escalating trade dispute between the U.S. and China.
U.S. Steel (X) is posting a particularly steep loss on the day despite reporting second quarter results that beat analyst estimates on both the top and bottom lines.
Significant weakness has also emerged among chemical stocks, as reflected by the 1.4 percent drop by the S&P Chemicals Index. DowDuPont (DWDP) is falling sharply even though the chemical giant reported better than expected second quarter results.
Oil stocks are also extending the sharp drop seen in the previous session, while notable strength is visible among telecom, biotechnology and computer hardware stocks.
Other Markets
In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved significantly lower during trading on Thursday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index slumped by 1 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index plunged by 2.2 percent.
The major European markets also moved to the downside on the day. While the German DAX Index sunk by 1.5 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index tumbled by 1 percent and the French CAC 40 Index fell by 0.7 percent.
In the bond market, treasuries are seeing modest strength following the drop seen in the previous session. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, is down by 1.9 basis points at 2.984 percent.
by RTTNews Staff Writer
